$comment: COPY THIS, then delete every $comment. It is a dataset document -- the thing
the validator checks and the only place a file's location is written down.
Generate the files[] entry rather than typing it:
$comment_ids: batch_id and lineage_id are NOT the same thing, and neither can be
reconstructed later -- which is why both are required now.
batch_id  : data that must never be split across a train/test boundary.
One synthesis batch. One catalyst charge. One beamtime.
lineage_id: data sharing a provenance chain. Repeated conditions, the same
sample measured across modalities, a trace and its reprocessing.
Two batches can share a lineage; one batch can span lineages.
$comment_status: 'ok' | 'flagged' | 'failed'. FLAG, NEVER DELETE. Anything other than 'ok'
requires a non-empty status_reason. A deleted failed run cannot be counted in
an exclusion table at manuscript time, and that table is a requirement.
$comment_autonomy: TRACE-AI scale A0-A5. This project is A1-A2, human-gated.
$comment_measurement: prbs_kinetics | ms | ir_gas | ir_transient | xas_mes | steady_state |
characterization | computational. Every experimental type must also declare
$comment_sample: The lab's OWN label, verbatim -- what is written on the vial. A
project-assigned relabelling scheme that disagrees with the physical label
is a scheme that gets ignored. This is the join key between kinetics,
spectroscopy, and characterization of the same material.
$comment_instrument: identifier must be stable across runs: it is what joins a dataset to the
$comment_channels: Units and uncertainty are required PER CHANNEL, so a channel cannot exist
with a unit and no uncertainty. quantity is what distinguishes a raw ion
current from a derived concentration -- do not write 'concentration' here
unless a calibration was actually applied, in which case layer is 'derived'
$comment_files: Exactly ONE of path, url, or lfs_oid per entry. When a set outgrows the
repository, REPLACE path with url -- do not add it alongside. The checksum is
what proves the bytes did not change, so every downstream consumer keeps
$comment_protocol: waveform is REQUIRED for prbs, in one of three forms -- lfsr (shown here),
recorded (the executed switch_times_s), or reconstructed (recovered from a
tracer, with the reason no better record exists). See protocols/_example.json
t0 must be UTC with an explicit offset. Three institutions in two time zones
plus a synchrotron cannot align transients on a wall clock. It may be omitted
only for legacy data that never recorded one, and then t0_absent_reason says
so -- do not omit it for data you are acquiring now.
If your instrument timestamps each species separately -- a scanning quadrupole
does -- set time_base.kind to per_channel and give each channel its own
time_column, rather than pretending they share one.
$comment_access: internal (project only) | staged (manuscript in preparation) | public.
This field, not repository visibility, is what governs release.
$comment_provenance: Normally written by the tool, not by hand. Hand-authored raw-layer datasets
are the exception, since there was no tool run to record.
$comment_calibration_ref: For a DERIVED dataset: art://<calibration-id>. Required in practice, because
a derived trace that does not cite its sensor model cannot be re-derived when
notes: REPLACE. Pretreatment history, reactor conditioning, deviations from protocol, and anything that went wrong. Optional, and the field most worth filling in -- this context is routinely essential to interpreting a catalysis experiment and routinely absent from structured fields. The validator warns when it is empty.
